A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same structured-QP/SVM research, retaining matching core algorithms and proofs despite the changed title and expanded scope. All 62 pages of v1 and 81 pages of v2 support comparison; neither contains a separately labeled appendix.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, mathematical formulations, complexity bounds, and proofs, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. Its added Gaussian-kernel algorithms and hardness constructions do not report experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Section 10 adds a Gaussian-kernel SVM procedure that constructs an approximate low-rank kernel, incorporates labels through diagonal scaling, and solves the resulting proxy QP with an allocated approximation error. This extends v1's procedures for supplied low-rank or low-treewidth objectives; the underlying QP/IPM algorithms remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or empirical evaluation. The added Gaussian-kernel input families and hardness instances are theoretical constructions, not evaluated task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. References to LIBSVM, other SVM solvers, and newly discussed kernel algorithms are theoretical or bibliographic comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. The new accuracy, dimension, and radius conditions belong to mathematical guarantees rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. The new radius-dependent complexity analysis consists of theoretical arguments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repetitions, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. Randomized-algorithm success probabilities and expected runtimes are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured scores, timings, rankings, or qualitative evaluation outcomes. Added and revised asymptotic complexity bounds are assessed under T1 and C1.

T1.justification: New Section 10 supplies kernel-approximation lemmas, the algorithmic guarantee and proof in Theorem 10.7, a Hamming-nearest-neighbor hardness reduction, and biased/soft-margin corollaries. Theorem 4.2 also changes the reported tree-decomposition time from soft-O(n+m) to O(m^(1+o(1))). The detailed core QP bounds, including Theorem 7.1, are largely retained.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's structured-QP/SVM claims, v2 claims an almost-linear Gaussian-kernel SVM algorithm for d=Theta(log n) and B=o(log n/log log n), together with improved SETH-based hardness bounds distinguishing biased and unbiased SVMs. The introductory treewidth-QP claim also drops the m << tau restriction and changes its runtime dependence on m (v1 Theorem 1.4; v2 Theorem 1.5).

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of why dense kernels and high-treewidth sparsifiers limit direct application of the retained solvers. Sections 2.4 and 3 discuss dimension/radius restrictions, the remaining algorithm–hardness gap, and limitations involving rank and constraint counts, substantially expanding v1's narrow discussion of a Lee–Sidford-barrier extension.

D1.justification: No software release, hardware information, experimental implementation settings, or code/data access instructions are added. Existing Algorithms 1–20 retain their substantive procedures; the new kernel construction is documented mathematically rather than through implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: v2 introduces a substantial kernel-matrix-algebra discussion citing AA22, ACSS20, BIMW21, BIK+23, and related KDE work, and develops a claimed improvement over the already cited BIS17 hardness result. It removes the treewidth-related-work paragraph and DLY21 citations, with much IPM attribution shifting to Ye20 and LV21.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, technique overview, and discussion are extensively rewritten, including expanded explanations of retained algorithms. v2 adds a contents section, reorganizes the SVM motivation, and revises notation throughout the SVM and low-rank sections; this exceeds changes attributable solely to the new theory.

P2.justification: v2 adds a contents display and revises captions and placement of existing algorithm boxes, including Algorithms 1, 2, 4, 6, and 10. The single-column mathematical presentation remains similar, with no new scientific figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves exposition and develops a substantial kernel-SVM extension, but important support issues make the net quality change uncertain. Section 2.4 claims multiplicative spectral approximation, whereas Lemma 10.5 establishes additive error; Theorem 10.7 does not establish that its proxy matrix remains positive semidefinite before invoking the convex solver. The strengthened introductory Theorem 1.5 also does not match the retained detailed bound in Theorem 7.1. These issues affect central claims, preventing a confident overall improvement judgment.
